notes: Trial prepared September 25, 2026 from the reviewed Mesa collection and its saved reconciled browser state. Later browser edits are not represented. Saved human exclusions are respected.
The order suggests which resources to curate first. It is not a provider rating or a referral order for every client. Each set deliberately mixes different help and practical alternatives.

All candidates assigned to these categories were compared using their saved descriptions; shortlisted records were read in full, and consequential uncertainties received targeted source checks. This is a selection trial, not a fresh verification of every provider or a new whole-office review.

Expand the saved records to inspect supporting information. They retain the previous four-section format; conversion to Stephanie's five sections belongs to the next preparation implementation. Original records and approval state have not been changed.
A New Leaf's ambiguous work-clothing/Autumn House identity is not selected. Potential duplicate records are identified in the assessment list rather than treated as extra provider capacity.

The four trial category IDs match the office list supplied by Claude. Other Mesa category differences still require explicit reconciliation before a production import. This trial uses existing IDs and cannot be imported as prepared resources.

checks.label: ARM of Save the Family
checks.finding: The official page says new waitlist applications are temporarily closed. Removed from the proposed starter set; retained as a future housing option, not deleted or treated as a closed organization.

checks.label: AllThrive transportation
checks.finding: The current page describes West Valley transportation. It does not establish Mesa coverage for this saved lead. Held outside the starter set pending a program-specific Mesa access check.

checks.label: Housing for Heroes
checks.finding: The official page identifies veteran housing support in Maricopa, Pinal and Yuma counties. Current intake and financial assistance remain subject to screening and funds.

checks.label: WE-CYCLE-USA
checks.finding: The official site describes bicycles and repairs for people in need, an earn-a-bike route, and appointment-based access. Confirm a working shop location and appointment; the published address should not be assumed a walk-in shop.

checks.label: Legal Assistance for Renters
checks.finding: The county page continues to identify CLS assistance for qualifying tenants facing nonpayment eviction. It does not establish acceptance of an individual case.

checks.label: Matthew's Crossing
checks.finding: The official site describes school-year weekend backpacks and campus food closets. The current Mesa school roster and referral process still need confirmation.

checks.label: La Mesa Resource Center
checks.finding: The official page describes personal help with identification documents, applications, and mail. Fee funding and current bus-pass stock remain separate questions.

checks.label: City of Mesa housing
checks.finding: The city identifies its security-deposit assistance program. This supports the pathway, not a guarantee of an open application window or funds.

checks.label: Valley Metro RideChoice
checks.finding: Direct page access was blocked by the research tool. This is not evidence of closure. Retain the reviewed program distinctions and require confirmation of Mesa-specific eligibility before curation.

categories.rationale: Nine selections address keeping housing, move-in costs, and shelter access for families, single men, single women, survivors, pregnant women and veteran households. Separate intake programs are retained even when operated by the same organization. A coordinated-entry record is not counted as an additional supply of beds.
categories.gaps: No immediately open general affordable-housing waitlist is established. Youth-only housing, recovery housing and additional rent providers remain in the reserve. ARM's closed waitlist should be revisited later. Shelter capacity, referral routes and funding must be checked; these selections are useful curation targets, not guaranteed placements.

members.label: MesaCAN — rent assistance
members.contribution: Starts with Mesa's own rent-assistance intake, helping eligible households preserve housing before shelter becomes necessary.
members.limitation: City of Mesa eligibility and limited appointment releases apply. Confirm the rent-intake schedule and funds; utility intake uses a different route.

evidence.text: MesaCAN rent and utility assistance

members.label: Community Legal Services — Legal Assistance for Renters
members.contribution: Adds legal screening and possible representation for nonpayment eviction, a different intervention from paying rent or finding a bed.
members.limitation: Case eligibility and acceptance need screening. Confirm current intake and any deadlines directly; assistance is not guaranteed.

evidence.text: CLS advice, negotiation, and court representation

members.label: Family Housing Hub — family shelter access
members.contribution: Provides a coordinated shelter-access route for families with minor children, including a possible Mesa intake option.
members.limitation: Assessment does not guarantee a bed. Saved addresses and satellite schedules conflict; confirm the current intake route before travel.

evidence.text: Primary coordinated-entry pathway for families

members.label: East Valley Men's Center — A New Leaf
members.contribution: Adds a Mesa residential homelessness program for adult men, who do not fit the family-with-children pathway.
members.limitation: Prescreening and program rules apply. Confirm the destination; A New Leaf's administrative address is not the program's intake address.

evidence.text: Homeless adult men eligible for East Valley Men’s Center prescreening

members.label: UMOM — Halle Women's Center and shelter intake
members.contribution: Adds an explicit shelter pathway for single women, complementing the family Hub and men's program.
members.limitation: The saved record combines several UMOM programs. Confirm the single-women intake route and waiting list rather than assuming the family Hub handles every case.

evidence.text: Halle Women’s Center: Dedicated emergency shelter for single women

members.label: Sojourner Center — survivor housing and pet support
members.contribution: Adds confidential survivor housing and a distinct pet-support pathway, an important constraint that ordinary shelter listings may not address.
members.limitation: Phoenix-based; housing and pet placement have separate availability. Confirm intake and pet arrangements without publishing a confidential shelter location.

evidence.text: DV shelter plus transitional apartments and a dedicated pet companion program

members.label: City of Mesa — security-deposit assistance
members.contribution: Addresses the up-front cost of entering an eligible rental, which differs from rent-arrears assistance and shelter placement.
members.limitation: Confirm the application window, funding and timing before lease signing or occupancy. Landlord, inspection and income rules apply.

evidence.text: Pays the refundable portion of a rental security deposit

members.label: Housing for Heroes — veteran housing stabilization
members.contribution: Adds a separate provider and veteran-specific prevention or rehousing assistance for qualifying households.
members.limitation: SSVF eligibility, current intake and available funds must be screened; this is not a general rent fund.

evidence.text: Separate SSVF grantee covering Maricopa

members.label: Maggie's Place — maternity housing
members.contribution: Adds housing tailored to homeless pregnant adults, with parenting support beyond an ordinary emergency-shelter listing.
members.limitation: Program-specific safety and household rules can exclude applicants with other children in their care. Confirm eligibility and openings; home addresses can be confidential.

evidence.text: Housing and wraparound support for homeless pregnant women 18+

categories.rationale: Ten selections combine ongoing benefits, prepared meals, take-home groceries, school food and delivery. Several local providers remain so referrals are not concentrated at one pantry; each alternative changes geography, access or the kind of food help.
categories.gaps: Confirm dietary accommodations, pantry schedules and current delivery boundaries. Summer-only school meals and additional neighborhood pantries remain in reserve. Meals to Grow needs its current Mesa school/referral list before office approval.

members.contribution: Adds ongoing grocery purchasing support, reducing dependence on repeated emergency pantry visits for eligible households.

categories.rationale: Nine selections distinguish general transit, fare assistance, travel training, health-plan rides, assisted senior rides, cancer and veteran transport, and bicycle access. Two bus-pass providers provide a practical alternative when supplies or outreach schedules differ.
categories.gaps: Affordable accessible nonmedical rides for people outside transit and volunteer eligibility remain difficult. AllThrive's current page does not establish Mesa coverage. No selected volunteer service guarantees urgent rides; separate Valley Metro program details need a clearer prepared record.

members.contribution: Provides the basic transit pathway plus reduced fares and separately eligible accessible-ride programs.
members.limitation: The record combines several programs and historical geography. Confirm Mesa-specific eligibility; a reduced bus fare does not establish RideChoice eligibility.

evidence.text: distinct public-transit, reduced-fare, ADA paratransit, RideChoice and commuter programs

evidence.text: administered through the member's specific managed care plan

evidence.text: Free volunteer-driver rides to and from cancer-related medical appointments

categories.rationale: Nine selections distinguish agencies that issue documents from local organizations that help clients obtain them. Three local assistance routes provide choices when evidence, fees, mailing address or schedules are the obstacle. National immigration and Social Security routes remain represented.
categories.gaps: Out-of-state birth certificates, military discharge records and corrections-specific release documents remain reserve pathways. Source records still need clearer descriptions of fees and alternative identity evidence. Tribal credentials apply only to that tribe's members.

members.label: Homeless ID Project — identification and document storage
members.contribution: Adds specialized no-cost help when homelessness or missing documents makes an ordinary agency application difficult.
members.limitation: Confirm the Mesa satellite schedule and holiday changes. The issuing agency still controls the document and timing.

evidence.text: replacement state IDs, driver's licenses, birth certificates and supporting documents at no cost

members.label: Paz de Cristo — ID vouchers, birth certificates and mail
members.contribution: Adds a Mesa route combining document help and mailing access, with the same resource also supporting food and transportation needs.
members.limitation: Each service has its own schedule and prerequisites. Confirm voucher availability and how someone without photo ID can access mail support.

evidence.text: Arizona ID vouchers, birth-certificate assistance

members.label: La Mesa Ministries — one-to-one document assistance
members.contribution: Adds another local navigator for forms, appointments and official mail when clients need assistance assembling an application.
members.limitation: Clarify which document fees can be funded. Navigation is not a promise that every document can be obtained free.

evidence.text: one-on-one help obtaining IDs, driver licenses, birth certificates, and Social Security cards

members.label: Arizona MVD — state ID issuance and replacement
members.contribution: Provides the official Arizona ID endpoint, which local assistance organizations help clients reach.
members.limitation: Confirm current documents and fee rules. General homelessness is not a blanket fee exemption, and Travel ID has separate requirements.

evidence.text: Arizona MVD state ID application and replacement

members.label: Maricopa County — Arizona vital records
members.contribution: Adds the official source for eligible Arizona birth-record requests, often part of rebuilding an identity-document chain.
members.limitation: Requester eligibility and identity evidence apply. It does not issue out-of-state records; the saved postal box is not a walk-in counter.

evidence.text: Official local source for certified birth and death certificates

members.label: Social Security Administration — replacement cards
members.contribution: Adds the federal Social Security card route, which MVD and county vital records cannot provide.
members.limitation: Confirm whether online replacement or an appointment applies. Use the current locator because saved local addresses conflict.

evidence.text: Official pathway for replacing a lost or stolen Social Security card

members.label: Immigrant Hope Mesa — immigration-document application help
members.contribution: Adds local low-cost assistance with supported immigration filings for clients who need help using the federal process.
members.limitation: Confirm fees and appointment availability. The record does not establish asylum or immigration-court representation.

evidence.text: green-card renewals/replacements

members.label: USCIS — replacement immigration documents
members.contribution: Adds the authoritative federal process for replacement immigration documents and temporary proof of status.
members.limitation: The correct form depends on the document. Biometrics centers are not general walk-in offices; appointment notices control destinations.

evidence.text: replacement permanent-resident cards, replacement naturalization/citizenship documents

members.contribution: Adds an otherwise unrepresented tribal-document pathway for enrolled community members living near Mesa.
members.limitation: This office serves its own enrolled members. People from other tribes need their tribe's enrollment office.

evidence.text: Enrolled Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community members
